summary: Test and ledger only, no src change. Forced the cross-wait on the app's own engine (writer holds the write lock on a pre-window connection, asks for a second one in the window): the probe's BEGIN IMMEDIATE (busy 30 s) waited 30.065 s and failed, the window was held 30.066 s, the writer's second open waited 29.767 s in connecting(); the repair declines writer-busy, nothing is switched. Control (the writer touches its first connection again): refused as stale, probe 0.33 s. Mechanism for the shipped app: repair.run holds the single-writer gate for the whole window, gated writers take the connection before the gate and hold the gate for their write transaction; the ungated corpus writers are kv saves (raw connect, outside the guard) and init DDL. Sweep over all 1,506 test files: 136,587 checkouts, 103,477 nested, 668 under a connection that had changed rows, all ORM sessions, none Core or raw. Windows restore file-step variant (handles, 300 s) named, not exercised. Two order tests, mutation-proved. Options named, none built: a shorter probe timeout; connecting() refusing at once a thread that already holds a connection of the engine.
